Treat ligand 2 as inspiration only: if you want to bring in one of its features, either call crossover_molecules to combine the two, or rebuild that feature yourself on your current working molecule (e.g. with add_substructure). An atom index you give to any tool other than crossover_molecules is always interpreted against your current working molecule, never against ligand 2 - do not reason about 'modifying ligand 2' and then call one of these tools, since the edit will land on the wrong molecule and likely do nothing you intended.

You are encouraged to make a crossover between the candidate molecules on the first step, then mutate the resulting molecule. Only make a few modifications (at most 3), then respond with FINAL ANSWER. Do not let molecular weight exceed 700.

Ligand 2 is the pool leader and I have already elaborated it; ligand 1 is the dimethoxybenzyl urea again, which is a convenient blank host - zero activity, but the best SA in the pool. Every NH-azine link I have installed so far has been a pyrimidine or a quinazoline, i.e. all azines of the same family, so I do not yet know whether the model is reading pyrimidine specifically or electron-poor N-heteroaryl-NH-aryl more generally. The cleanest way to separate those is a different heterocycle class entirely, so I am installing benzothiazol-2-ylamino: a 1,3-thiazole-fused azine, and the actual recognition element of AS601245, a bona fide JNK inhibitor. Step 1: the primary acetamide at atoms 15-18 is the throwaway piece (2 donors, TPSA 102.7, no benefit). Atom 14 is the aromatic carbon bearing it, the 14-15 bond is non-ring, so cut there and attach the N-linked 2-aminobenzothiazole.

Benzothiazole installed, SA still 2.01, but QED is down to 0.364 - at 435 Da with LogP 5.38 the molecule is well outside drug-like space, and the sulfur-rich fused ring is what pushed LogP there. Same remedy as before, and it is a large one here: atom 8 is the urea carbonyl and atom 7 is the NH linking it to the dimethoxybenzyl, a non-ring bond, so cutting it removes the NH, the CH2, the whole benzene and both methoxys - twelve atoms, about 165 Da - in a single modification. A methyl on the carbonyl leaves N-[4-(1,3-benzothiazol-2-ylamino)phenyl]acetamide at ~283 Da: LogP near 3.8, TPSA 68, 3 rotatable bonds, 2 donors. That is the clean two-link molecule with a thiazole-class azine instead of a pyrimidine, which is exactly the comparison this episode exists to make.
